status: block complete (mechanism/gluing). One proved obstruction set (Theorems A-C) + one pre-registered 1.24 s exact census on the validated 553-vertex graph. No new graph built, no variant hunting, no chi(R^2) claim.
summary: Asked whether an exact gluing of the validated point-graph pipeline can create a new colouring constraint. Theorem A: gluing over a CLIQUE interface with no cross edges cannot raise chi above max of the pieces - which is why every block-1 specimen sat at 3 or 4. Theorem B: a palette excluder for a non-adjacent pair lies in the intersection of two unit circles, so has at most 2 vertices, so palette exclusion forces equality only for k<=3; the diamond attains k=3, so this is sharp. Theorem C: a pair's two common neighbours are a unit edge iff |pq|^2=3, so the diamond is the unique 2-clique excluder. C's three predictions were verified exactly on the real 553-vertex 5-chromatic graph (0 K4, max 2 common neighbours over 149906 pairs, 7901 diamond pairs, 0 failures). The candidate non-clique sqrt3-pair gluing of two double-lenses is specified but NOT run: Theorem B says it cannot force, and it would be a block-1 variant. So the limitation is proved and the missing interface named: GADGET_k, a forced-equality pair not from a common neighbourhood; none known for k=4,5,6.
verified_results: GRADE [P] Theorem A (clique interface cannot increase chi). If G = G1 union G2 with V1 cap V2 = K inducing a clique and no edges between V1\K and V2\K, then chi(G) <= max(chi G1, chi G2). Proof: both colourings are injective on K, so a permutation of the colour set matches them on K; properness holds on each side and every edge lies on one side. Consequence: every block-1 specimen is an amalgam over clique interfaces, so its ceiling of 4 is a theorem, not a search artifact.

GRADE [P] Theorem B (palette-exclusion forcing dies at k=4). A palette excluder for a non-adjacent pair (a clique all of whose vertices are adjacent to both marks) lies in the intersection of two unit circles, hence has at most 2 vertices; so the forced palette has size >= k-2, and equality can be forced only for k <= 3. Sharp: the diamond attains k=3 (block-1 exact counts 6 vs 0). This is a statement about the MECHANISM only; it does not say no unit-distance graph forces equality at k>=4.

GRADE [P]+[A] Theorem C (diamond uniqueness). For non-adjacent p,q with exactly two common neighbours c1,c2, |c1c2|^2 = 4 - |pq|^2 exactly, so c1c2 is a unit edge iff |pq|^2 = 3. Equivalently the diamond is the only unit-distance configuration that excludes a 2-clique from a pair's palette. Geometric core checked in exact arithmetic (check_geometry.py, Q(sqrt3,sqrt5,sqrt11)): the only points at distance 1 from two vertices of a unit triangle are the third vertex itself (distance 0 from it) and its reflection (distance sqrt3 from it), so a unit triangle has no common unit neighbour at all.

GRADE [A] Pre-registered census on the validated 553-vertex 5-chromatic unit-distance graph, all three predictions held: P1 omega <= 3 (0 K4 witnesses, 1093 triangles, max clique 3); P2 every non-adjacent pair has at most 2 common neighbours (maximum 2 over 149906 pairs; histogram {0:132261, 1:9744, 2:7901}); P3 pairs with exactly 2 common neighbours satisfy |pq|^2 = 3 and are a unit edge (7901 pairs, 0 discriminations failed). Runtime 1.24 s, single process, cap 60 s. Artifact certs/census_heule553.json.

Corrected in fix_p1.py (a triangle plus a common neighbour adjacent to all three); the corrected count is 0. Recorded in certs/census_heule553.json under P1_note. GRADE [C] Inherited, kept separate: the 553-vertex 4-UNSAT control (block 2; DRAT certificate verified by drat-trim, s VERIFIED) and the block-1 counts/witnesses with the iff-k=3 diamond proposition. Nothing in this block depends on them beyond reusing the same validated coordinate file.
conjectures: Escape from Theorem B requires a CASCADE, not a bigger clique: the colour of p pinned by neighbours whose colours are themselves pinned, so the constraint arrives from graph distance >= 2. Named as the missing interface GADGET_k.
GADGET_4 (a forced-equality pair at 4 colours) most likely exists only well above 16 vertices; the two-double-lens sqrt3 gluing of 16 vertices is predicted 4-colourable and uninformative.

escalation.obstacle: GADGET_k: does there exist, for k = 4 (or 5, 6), a finite unit-distance graph G with two marks p,q at distance d != 1 such that G is k-colourable but G+pq is not, where the forcing does NOT come from a common neighbourhood of p and q? By Theorem B every common-neighbour palette in the plane has size >= k-2, so any such gadget must be a cascade of length >= 2. None is known for any k >= 4.
escalation.definitions: A unit-distance graph is a finite graph with an injection into R^2 such that uv is an edge iff |u-v| = 1. A proper k-colouring has c(u) != c(v) on every edge. The diamond is K_4 minus an edge: a,b,t1,t2 with edges ab, at1, at2, bt1, bt2 and |t1-t2| = sqrt3. A palette excluder for a non-adjacent pair (p,q) is a clique S with every s in S adjacent to both p and q.
escalation.hypotheses: Exact real-algebraic coordinates; complete finite graph; no measurability, periodicity or lattice hypothesis; no restriction to a specific number field.
escalation.attempted_approaches: Clique-interface gluing (killed by Theorem A); palette exclusion via common neighbours (killed at k>=4 by Theorem B, sharp at k=3 by the diamond); stacked/common-unit-neighbour iteration (the operation is an involution, block 1); exhaustive forced-pair census on the spindle family (nothing forced at k>=4); and now the mechanism cap verified at scale on a real 5-chromatic graph.
escalation.expected_useful_output: Either one explicit exact-coordinate cascade gadget of size <= 60 forcing equality at k=4 (then the same design pattern is the only plausible route to k=6, and the branch has a construction programme), or a theorem bounding the size of a cascade gadget needed to force at k from below by a function of k (for instance via the palette cap of Theorem B composed along a path of length L: state the exact list-size propagation and where it fails), together with the explicit radius at which exact enumeration of candidate cascades stops being feasible.
